description:
FOUND s494 (Fable, 2026-09-21) by the FAILURE-EXPERIENCE battery (questions-worth-asking Q5; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/q5/sig/{run-sig.pl,run-sig.log,selfsig.pl,h2.pl,pipe.pl}).  perl 5.40.3 vs main 863d3e20, the user-facing `pcl` command (same under ./runpcl).

MEASURED (external signal sent after the script printed "ready"):
    script                         signal   perl                         pcl
    while (1) { sleep }            INT      dies by signal 2, silent     exit 1, 32 stderr lines "Unhandled sb-sys:interactive-interrupt ... Backtrace"
    while (1) { sleep }            TERM     dies by signal 15, silent    exit 0, silent            <- a supervisor / `timeout` / systemd reads SUCCESS
    while (1) { sleep }            HUP      dies by signal 1             dies by signal 1          (same)
    $SIG{INT} = sub { print "caught INT\n"; exit 7 }    INT    "caught INT", exit 7      backtrace, exit 1 -- THE HANDLER NEVER RAN
    $SIG{TERM} = sub { print "caught TERM\n"; exit 8 }  TERM   "caught TERM", exit 8     exit 0, silent   -- THE HANDLER NEVER RAN (cleanup code: lock files, temp files, child reaping)
    self-signal: $SIG{INT}=sub{...}; kill "INT", $$;    -      "caught INT" and continues     backtrace, program dead
    print "line $_\n" for 1..200000; print STDERR "reached the end\n";   piped into `head -1`:
                                            perl: killed by SIGPIPE at once (pipeline status 13 / 141), stderr empty
                                            pcl : prints all 200000 lines into the closed pipe, "reached the end", rc 0 -- `while (1) { print ... }` | head NEVER terminates
MECHANISM (read): cl/pcl-runtime.lisp has exactly ONE `sb-sys:enable-interrupt` -- `%p-ensure-alarm-handler`, installed lazily by `alarm`, dispatching to (gethash "ALRM" %SIG).  %SIG is an ordinary hash (#1873 / #1029 note the same fact from the magic side: perl QUALIFIES a string handler name on store).  Nothing reads %SIG for any other signal, so SBCL's own dispositions stay in force.  INFERRED FROM THE MEASUREMENT, NOT READ IN SBCL'S SOURCE (take the discriminating measurement first: print the dispositions at boot with sb-unix / `sb-sys:enable-interrupt`'s return value, 3 minutes): SIGINT = SBCL's interactive-interrupt (-> the debugger hook -> backtrace, exit 1 -- this one is SEEN in the backtrace), SIGTERM = a handler that exits with code 0, SIGPIPE = ignored (write errors then go unnoticed by `print`, which would be why the producer runs on -- ALSO check whether `print`'s return value reports EPIPE today).  #2094 names HUP/USR1 only; this is the whole family and OWNS that half of #2094 (the `$$`-stale half stays there).  #1928 (op/sigdispatch.t: NUL-clean lookups, deferral inside a handler) is downstream of this.

FIX SHAPE (one mechanism, three consumers; right layer = runtime, genuine perl core semantics):
1. STORE-MAGIC ON %SIG (the box-magic hook precedent, docs/ir-spec + [[reference_box_magic_hook]]; the hash-level equivalent): a store of a CODE ref / sub NAME under a real signal name installs `sb-sys:enable-interrupt SIGNO` with ONE dispatcher lambda that looks the handler up AT DELIVERY (so a later reassignment needs no re-install) and calls it with the signal NAME as $_[0]; "IGNORE" -> :ignore; "DEFAULT" / undef / delete / `local` restore -> perl's default disposition.  The same store is where #1873's name qualification belongs (rule 11: one seam).  `local $SIG{INT} = ...` must restore the previous disposition on scope exit -- probe it.
2. PERL'S DEFAULT DISPOSITIONS AT BOOT, in the ONE place every runner shares (the runtime's init hook, not the `pcl` script): INT and TERM with no perl handler = die BY THE SIGNAL, quietly (restore SIG_DFL and re-raise, so the shell sees 130 / 143 and END blocks policy matches perl: perl does NOT run END on a default-disposition signal death); PIPE = SIG_DFL (perl's default; with it `print` to a closed pipe kills the producer quietly, which is what makes `| head` work).  The TEST runners rely on today's behaviour in places -- measure: `timeout`'s TERM against the gate/sweep children (a TERM that now kills by signal instead of exit 0 changes how a TIMEOUT is recorded? read tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl + run-perl-suite.pl's status decoding FIRST), and `Pl/t/transpile-test-06.t`'s %SIG pre-population row ([[feedback_never_nohup_the_gate]]).
3. DELIVERY: SBCL runs the lambda asynchronously in the main thread unless interrupts are disabled; perl's "safe signals" deliver between ops.  A handler that `die`s must unwind out of a blocking read/sleep (ALRM already does -- same path).  A signal arriving INSIDE a handler is deferred (#1928).  `sleep` / `select` interrupted by a handled signal return early (#2002 is s492c's, same edit family -- read its result first).
WHAT COULD BREAK: `alarm` + `$SIG{ALRM}` (route it through the new seam or prove the two coexist); fork children (a child inherits the dispositions -- docs/not-supported.md ~line 1359 "child inherits SBCL's signal handlers ... `$? & 127` can read 0 where perl shows the signal": this fix should make that entry SMALLER -- re-probe and edit it); `kill 0, $pid`; `$SIG{CHLD} = "IGNORE"` (auto-reap) and `$SIG{CHLD} = sub { wait }`; `%SIG` enumerated (`keys %SIG` lists every signal name in perl -- the gate row knows); the XS bridge; SBCL's own use of signals (stop-the-world GC uses a signal on threaded builds, and the write barrier / guard pages use SIGSEGV / SIGBUS; WHICH signal stop-for-GC is differs by platform and SBCL version and Fable did NOT verify it -- find it in the running image, e.g. `sb-unix::sig-stop-for-gc` if present; perl programs DO use USR1 / USR2, so this matters -- never let a perl handler take a signal SBCL's runtime owns: a closed DENY list, rule 12: a handler for such a signal ANNOUNCES once and is not installed).
PORTABILITY (USER standing): signal NUMBERS differ between Linux and macOS -- names map through sb-unix / sb-posix constants, never literals; the install matrix + a macOS leg are part of the bar.  This is PLATFORM-TOUCHING.
BAR: a new Pl/t signal file (self-signal rows are deterministic: `kill "USR1", $$` with a handler; external-signal rows through the helper that waits for "ready"); companion op/sigdispatch.t op/alarm.t op/kill0.t op/fork.t op/sigsystem.t io/pipe.t by ROWS; the q5 sig battery before -> after; full sweep (cl/ change) with the TIMEOUT accounting re-read; ir-spec (normative: the %SIG contract).
SIZE: one agent-day, design above; Fable reviews the DENY list and the boot dispositions before merge.


=== THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, TAKEN (Fable, s494; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/q5/sig/sigmask.pl reads SigIgn / SigCgt from /proc/self/status INSIDE the running program) ===
    perl:  SigIgn = FPE                                   SigCgt = (nothing)
    pcl :  SigIgn = PIPE                                  SigCgt = INT ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE SEGV USR2 ALRM TERM CHLD URG
So the inferences above are now FACTS for SBCL 2.6.0 on Linux x86-64: SIGPIPE is IGNORED (a write to a closed pipe returns EPIPE and nothing stops the producer); INT and TERM are CAUGHT by SBCL's own handlers (interactive-interrupt -> backtrace; terminate -> exit 0); and the RUNTIME-OWNED set -- the DENY list a perl handler must never take over -- is, on this build, **ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE SEGV USR2 URG** (synchronous faults, the GC's stop signal, and one SBCL uses internally).  **USR2 is the one that matters: perl programs use it**, so `$SIG{USR2} = sub {...}` must ANNOUNCE once on stderr and not install (rule 12's effect-only boundary), with a not-supported.md line.  HUP USR1 QUIT WINCH CONT TSTP TTIN TTOU VTALRM PROF IO are FREE.  CHLD is caught by SBCL (run-program's child bookkeeping): a perl `$SIG{CHLD}` handler must CHAIN to SBCL's, or PCL's own `system` / piped opens lose their exit statuses.  ALRM is caught before any `alarm` call (SBCL's timer machinery) and `%p-ensure-alarm-handler` replaces it lazily -- route ALRM through the new seam and probe that `sb-ext:timer` users inside the runtime (if any: grep) still work.
DERIVE THE DENY LIST FROM THE RUNNING IMAGE AT BOOT (read the caught set before PCL installs anything: /proc is Linux-only, so use sb-unix / sigaction through sb-alien to ask for each signal's current disposition -- portable to macOS), never from a literal list: it differs by platform and SBCL version.
BRIEF: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/s494g/prompt.md (label s494g, IDs 2260-2274, runtime-only).


=== s494g STEP 1: HOW EACH RUNNER DECODES A CHILD'S EXIT, BEFORE -> AFTER (written before the disposition change) ===
Measured on 40da28bd with three scratch files (a hang, a self-INT, a self-TERM; logs scratch/s494g/runner-sweep-{before,after}.log) and by reading the decode lines.
GNU timeout(1): a TIMED-OUT child makes timeout exit 124 WHATEVER the child did with the TERM (measured: `timeout 1 perl -e "sleep 3"` -> 124<<8), so a hung SBCL that dies BY SIGNAL 15 after the change is still 124.  A child that dies of its own signal N makes timeout exit N (measured: raw 15<<8 / 2<<8).  dash (`/bin/sh`) reports a signal death of a forked command as an ordinary exit 128+N (measured raw 36608 = 143<<8), so a wrapper that runs SBCL through `system("... 2>file")` could not tell a signal death from an exit.
  runner                      decode                                       case                  BEFORE (40da28bd)                                AFTER (s494g)
  tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl   timeout ... ; ($?>>8)==124 -> TIMEOUT;        hung file             SBCL exit 0 on TERM, timeout 124 -> TIMEOUT     SBCL dies by 15, timeout 124 -> TIMEOUT (unchanged)
                              else !=0 -> CRASH; short TAP -> PARTIAL       test dies by INT      backtrace, exit 1 -> CRASH (errline "Unhandled sb-sys:interactive-interrupt")   dies by 2, timeout exits 2 -> CRASH (no errline)
                                                                           test dies by TERM     SBCL exit 0 -> PARTIAL                           dies by 15 -> CRASH
  tools/run-perl-suite.pl     timeout -k 10; ($?>>8)==124 -> TIMEOUT;       hung file             TIMEOUT                                          TIMEOUT (unchanged; the -k KILL is no longer needed for a TERM-deaf SBCL)
                              otherwise status from TAP counts only         signal death          verdict by rows (exit ignored)                   same
  tools/pclperl-for-tests     system("sbcl ... 2> err"); ($?>>8)&0xFF       child dies by N       dash exit 128+N -> wrapper exit 128+N; a perl test reads $?&127 = 0   `exec sbcl`; a signal death is RE-RAISED (PCLSbcl::exit_like) -> $?&127 = N like perl
  ./runpcl                    system("sbcl ... 2>err"); $?>>8              child dies by N       exit 128+N (a -9 read "rc=137" only by accident of the shell)   re-raised: dies by N
  ./pcl                       exec sbcl                                    any                   the real status (right before and after)          same
  Pl/t/PCLCore.pm             transpile only (no SBCL run status)          -                     -                                                -
So the TIMEOUT label cannot move; what moves is a test file that DIES BY A SIGNAL: INT stays CRASH (quieter), TERM moves PARTIAL -> CRASH (it was a silent exit 0 before, which is exactly the #2107 bug).

EPIPE; numbers from sb-unix/sb-posix BY NAME.
